CAR TROUBLE

By: Ntokozo Miya | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We expose the workings of a family that operates numerous dodgy dealerships across Gauteng, leaving their customers out of cash and/or without the cars they were trying to sell or buy.

Unique Selling Point:
Using hidden camera footage, we show how one car is sold to multiple customers, without the necessary registration and ownership documents.

Summary:
At the beginning of the year, a group of about 50 customers of various connected car dealerships took to Facebook to complain about bad experiences when they tried to sell cars to and buy cars from the businesses. The complaints range from people who bought cars but did not receive ownership papers as well as others who handed their cars to dealerships to be sold but were never given money from those sales. The disgruntled customers found that the owner of some of the dealerships is Rajen Pillay who has brothers, Clinton Pillay and Dillan Ankiah, who also own car dealerships. Rajen's main dealership has had as many as 4 business names in the last few years – this is supposedly because when people start frequenting the dealership with their grievances and demands, Rajen simply renovates the store and gives it a new name, placing one of his other relatives or acquantances at the front desk. The same goes for Clinton and Dillan at their dealerships. When customers confronted Rajen about getting their money or cars back, Rajen made numerous payment arrangements with some of them but did not honour any of the agreements.

Further information:
Some customers have opened cases with the SAPS but there has been no arrests or even any movement in the cases while others have approached their lawyers. Till today, Rajen, Clinton and Dillan remain free and continue to operate car shops at other locations. The National Consumer Commission is familiar with such dodgy dealerships and calls them 'park and sell' schemes. We have joined the victims' WhatsApp group which currently has about 60 participants.

Also, we went undercover and found a vehicle that belongs to our case study Terri Dicks put up for sale at a newly set-up dealership in Meyerton.

Script:


CAR TROUBLE – DRAFT 21

PROMO 1 - Angry customers are scrambling to get their money and cars back after they were cheated by a Gauteng network of dealerships that promised them sweet deals on used vehicles.
PROMO 2 - Cars sold without papers or even permission from the owners, a single vehicle sold to multiple buyers – customers accuse a family dealership of doing dodgy business.
PROMO 3 - Angry customers of a network of used-car dealerships in Gauteng say they were promised sweet deals but were instead cheated out of cash and their vehicles.

AUDIO
LINK – In these tough economic times, more people choose pre-owned vehicles when shopping for a ride, while many who are strapped for cash, sell their used vehicles to dealerships across the country.
VO – But for some customers of a network of used-car dealerships in Gauteng, the sweet deals they were promised, instead left them out of pocket and out of the driver's seat.
TERRI DICKS – NISSAN NAVARA OWNER
There are no words for how they have deliberately cheated people, stolen from people
VO – In a WhatsApp group of nearly sixty people, Rajen Pillay and his associates Nesan Naicker and Dillan Ankiah, who work at used car dealerships in the south of Joburg, are accused of selling cars with no registration papers and without the consent of the owners.
Randy Fritz, who sold his 2008 BMW 330i to Rajen at Cars at Ridgeway in 2014, says the dealers move around various locations and often change the dealership names.
RANDY FRITZ – BMW 330i OWNER
I think they're dodging the people that they've actually conned. So people think that it's new owners because it's a new name.
VO - The CIPC, which registers companies shows that Rajen Pillay, real name Sadhasivan Pillay, was a director at Red Cars, which changed its name to Cars at Ridgeway.
Rajen told us that he and other partners were the owners of Hi Brid Auto, a business registered as Hi-Brid Auctioneers which also operates from the same premises as Cars at Ridgeway. On the day Mohapi Mphaki went to sell his 2003 VW Jetta to Hi-Brid Auto in 2018, he says he dealt with Nesan and a female consultant.
MOHAPI MPHAKI – VW JETTA OWNER
After selling that car, I wanted to invest in another business which will help me with my studies. We agreed on R50k. It's been a year, I have never received any money from them.
VO - Nesan Naicker is a director of CarBar, said to have recently moved from Lenasia to Ridgeway – the same address that is currently listed as that of Cars at Ridgeway and Hi Brid Auto.
Rajen says that he sublets the premises to Car Bar.
TERRI DICKS – NISSAN NAVARA OWNER
We dealt with Dillan from day one.
VO - Dillan Ankiah, who allegedly introduced himself as Dillan Pillay to some customers, was working at another dealership in Randburg when Terri Dicks first met him in July 2018.
She wanted to sell her bakkie, similar to this one, and replace it with a Mercedes Benz CLC200.
TERRI DICKS – NISSAN NAVARA OWNER
The bakkie was very heavy on fuel so we decided to have the Merc instead.
VO – Terri owed R125 000 on the financed bakkie. And until she settled the outstanding amount, the vehicle belonged to the bank. Terri says Dillan told her that he had moved to Hi-Brid, his brother Rajen's dealership and said they would take the bakkie off her hands.
TERRI DICKS – NISSAN NAVARA OWNER
They then gave me a letter that they will settle the bakkie. They never honoured that. They ran away with the bakkie.
VO – Dillon allegedly sold the vehicle, but Terri didn’t receive any of the money. She was forced to continue repaying the loan on a bakkie no longer in her possession.
LINK – Selling a car that isn't fully paid off at the bank is a huge risk and is not encouraged by motor industry experts.
VO – Wendy Knowler is a consumer rights journalist and activist – she says there are warning signs for consumers when doing business with dealerships.
WENDY KNOWLER – CONSUMER RIGHTS EXPERT
You need to inform your bank. If the bank doesn't do business with that dealership, then that's a clue right there that this isn't a good way for you to go.
VO – At the time that Terri put her bakkie up for sale, financing for the Mercedes Benz she wanted, was already confirmed. To Terri’s surprise, the Mercedes was delivered on a flatbed truck.
WENDY KNOWLER - CONSUMER RIGHTS EXPERT
Trust me that cost them money – why would they incur that extra cost for any other reason than the car is actually such a dud that it's not driveable.
VO – Terri took the car straight to a mechanic – it had numerous faults that she says neither Dillan nor Rajen had disclosed.
TERRI DICKS – NISSAN NAVARA OWNER
We left the car there and I phoned Dillan and I phoned the brother. I said: “Best you go and collect it because I'm not going to continue with this finance.”
VO – But by then, her bank had already paid the dealership for the Merc. Terri alleges that Dillan collected the car from the mechanic and promised to fix or replace it.
TERRI DICKS – NISSAN NAVARA OWNER
They sold it to us for R200 000 and obviously it escalated to R269 000.

VO – That was the last time Terri saw the Merc. In total, Terri now owes three hundred and ninety four thousand rands for the two cars. And whomever is currently using the bakkie seems like a loose cannon on the roads.
TERRI DICKS – NISSAN NAVARA OWNER

The fines started coming in one after the other. The fines are sitting close on R10 000.
VO - Unlike Terri though, Randy did get money for his car, but not all of it. Of the R200 000 he expected from Cars at Ridgeway after selling his car to Rajen, he only got R62 500.
RANDY FRITZ – BMW 330i OWNER
When you get there, they give you stories, like, they were waiting for a payment from a certain person and that person didn't pay so now they can't pay you.If you're paying off R200 000 in the form of a R1 000 every few months, how long is going to take them to pay you?
VO – Randy engaged lawyers, but even a court ruling in his favour didn't motivate the dealership to pay him.
Other disgruntled vehicle owners shared photos of their cars on social media hoping to track down the people who bought them.
Customers had information that the Pillays had moved their business to Meyerton, more than fifty kilometres away from Johannesburg.
So, our undercover operative went car shopping at the Meyerton dealership.
The new set-up showcases around twenty vehicles. Among them a sleek black Mercedes Benz CLC200 – Terri's car, recognizable by its registration number from her original documents.
The salesperson is none other than Dillan – the same Dillan who allegedly sold the car to Terri and later took it back for repairs.
UPSOUND
CB – What I want to know is – do you have a spare key?
DILLAN – A spare key, we don't guarantee you but I can check for you if there is a spare key or not.
WENDY KNOWLER – CONSUMER RIGHTS EXPERT
If you are buying a second-hand car and they tell you that they don't have a spare key to give you right then and there, please walk away from the deal.
UPSOUND
CB – So, you said you're fixing the papers...
DILLAN – Everything I'll do now and when you come through with the proof of payment, then I will be able to do a sale agreement for you.






VO – Essentially, Dillan is selling the same vehicle for a second time, and without Terri or the bank's permission.
According to the National Consumer Act, a consumer is someone who buys goods, not a seller, so the National Consumer Commission, which protects the rights of consumers, has no jurisdiction over conflicts where someone sells a car to a dealership and is not paid.
Eighteen of the people in the WhatsApp group have opened police cases against Rajen, Dillan and Nesan. Brigadier Mathapelo Peters followed up on the status of the cases.
BRIG. MATHAPELO PETERS – SOUTH AFRICAN POLICE SERVICES
Over 80% of them have been returned from the prosecutor and the decision of the prosecutor was that they were civil matters. However, given that the police have picked up a number of concerning common denominators, a team has been assigned to look again at these dockets. In fact, over 60 of the dockets are sitting in the detective's offices where they have been instructed to re-investigate.
VO – No arrests have been made.
LINK – We are taking a drive to Meyerton to confront Dillan about selling Terri's car without her permission.
VO – When Dillan saw the cameras he broke into a sprint but couldn't outrun our crew.
UPSOUND
MASA - Why are you selling Terri Dicks car and several other people's cars without their permission? Are you running a legitimate business here, and if you are, you would have responded to these questions? So you understand that what you are doing is illegal? Does Terri know that her car is on sale?
DILLAN – You are speaking to the wrong person?
MASA – Your name is Dillan, we're speaking to the right person. We already have you on spycam trying to sell this car? (Dillan drives off) Oh well, there you have it, that speaks volumes?
LINK - So the good news is, we found Terri's car and the bad news is Dillan refused to answer any of our questions or explain why he's operating illegally.
VO - We called the Pillay brothers and their associates for their side of the story, but all their known contact numbers either went to voicemail or were unanswered. We left messages.
Only Rajen called us back but refused to be on camera. He sent a lengthy response through his attorney.
His broad explanation for cars sold without papers is that it is likely that those cars were sold “voetstoots” – meaning they were sold without guarantee or warranty.
TERRI DICKS – NISSAN NAVARA OWNER
We then tried to track him down. Eventually, he started blocking our calls and wouldn't take our calls



VO - To suggestions that the business changed its name often to avoid irate customers, he responded that “that inference...is ludicrous and baseless” and Rajen says if it was his intention to evade clients, he would have left the province or the suburb, “and not occupied the same premises”.
Rajen says “the obligations due to Randy were erroneously overlooked” and that he and his partners in the business were committed to a payment plan in this regard.
RANDY FRITZ – BMW 330 OWNER
A lot of people trusted them and this gave me a sense of security, if you want to call it that, and that was my biggest mistake.
VO - Despite the fact that Mohapi's sale documents are on a Hi-Brid letterhead, Rajen wrote that Mohapi actually did business with Car Bar, which is not owned by him. He went on to say that Car Bar have assured him that they would be attending to the matter immediately.
MOHAPI MPHAKI – VW JETTA OWNER
To be honest, I don't have hope. He's happy, he's living his life but we are suffering.
VO – Rajen is doing his own investigation into Terri's allegations and says he will “ensure that any agreement legitimately entered into between her and Hi-Brid Auto will be attended to in due course” including the traffic fines accrued onto her name.
TERRI DICKS – NISSAN NAVARA OWNER
I have stopped the debit order on the bank which is obviously not conducive to a business woman like me, having almost been blacklisted.
VO – Rajen says he has “thousands of satisfied customers” and that it is unfortunate that we are only focusing on the “+/- 1.5% who've had an “unsatisfactory experience.”

LINK - So the good news is, we found Terri's car and the bad news is Dillan refused to answer any of our questions or explain why he's operating illegally. VO - We called the Pillay brothers and their associates for their side of the story, but all their known contact numbers either went to voicemail or were unanswered. We left messages. Only Rajen called us back but refused to be on camera. He sent a lengthy response through his attorney. His broad explanation for cars sold without papers is that it is likely that those cars were sold “voetstoots” – meaning they were sold without guarantee or warranty. TERRI DICKS – NISSAN NAVARA OWNER We then tried to track him down. Eventually, he started blocking our calls and wouldn't take our calls VO - To suggestions that the business changed its name often to avoid irate customers, he responded that “that inference...is ludicrous and baseless” and Rajen says if it was his intention to evade clients, he would have left the province or the suburb, “and not occupied the same premises”. Rajen says “the obligations due to Randy were erroneously overlooked” and that he and his partners in the business were committed to a payment plan in this regard. RANDY FRITZ – BMW 330 OWNER A lot of people trusted them and this gave me a sense of security, if you want to call it that, and that was my biggest mistake. VO - Despite the fact that Mohapi's sale documents are on a Hi-Brid letterhead, Rajen wrote that Mohapi actually did business with Car Bar, which is not owned by him. He went on to say that Car Bar have assured him that they would be attending to the matter immediately. MOHAPI MPHAKI – VW JETTA OWNER To be honest, I don't have hope. He's happy, he's living his life but we are suffering. VO – Rajen is doing his own investigation into Terri's allegations and says he will “ensure that any agreement legitimately entered into between her and Hi-Brid Auto will be attended to in due course” including the traffic fines accrued onto her name. TERRI DICKS – NISSAN NAVARA OWNER I have stopped the debit order on the bank which is obviously not conducive to a business woman like me, having almost been blacklisted. VO – Rajen says he has “thousands of satisfied customers” and that it is unfortunate that we are only focusing on the “+/- 1.5% who've had an “unsatisfactory experience.”

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We expose the workings of a family that operates numerous dodgy dealerships across Gauteng, leaving their customers out of cash and/or without the cars they were trying to sell or buy.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Using hidden camera footage, we show how one car is sold to multiple customers, without the necessary registration and ownership documents.
metadata.Summary: At the beginning of the year, a group of about 50 customers of various connected car dealerships took to Facebook to complain about bad experiences when they tried to sell cars to and buy cars from the businesses. The complaints range from people who bought cars but did not receive ownership papers as well as others who handed their cars to dealerships to be sold but were never given money from those sales. The disgruntled customers found that the owner of some of the dealerships is Rajen Pillay who has brothers, Clinton Pillay and Dillan Ankiah, who also own car dealerships. Rajen's main dealership has had as many as 4 business names in the last few years – this is supposedly because when people start frequenting the dealership with their grievances and demands, Rajen simply renovates the store and gives it a new name, placing one of his other relatives or acquantances at the front desk. The same goes for Clinton and Dillan at their dealerships. When customers confronted Rajen about getting their money or cars back, Rajen made numerous payment arrangements with some of them but did not honour any of the agreements.
metadata.Further information: Some customers have opened cases with the SAPS but there has been no arrests or even any movement in the cases while others have approached their lawyers. Till today, Rajen, Clinton and Dillan remain free and continue to operate car shops at other locations. The National Consumer Commission is familiar with such dodgy dealerships and calls them 'park and sell' schemes. We have joined the victims' WhatsApp group which currently has about 60 participants. Also, we went undercover and found a vehicle that belongs to our case study Terri Dicks put up for sale at a newly set-up dealership in Meyerton.
